title: Optimal bounds on the classical value of the repeated CHSH game
abstract: We show that the maximum winning probability in the repeated CHSH game for classical strategies is at most $\left(\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{4}\right)^n$. Together with a matching lower bound by Barak et al. (FOCS'2008), this determines the asymptotic value of the repeated CHSH game exactly. We also show that, if an XOR game has a gap between classical and quantum values, there is also a gap between the asymptotic values for the repeated game.
summary: This paper rigorously determines the exact asymptotic rate for the repeated CHSH game, showing it is $1 +  rac{\sqrt{5}}{4}$. By analyzing relaxations on the optimization problem, the authors prove that a gap exists between the classical and quantum bounds even in the limit of many repetitions. This confirms the non-local nature of quantum correlations.
main_problem: The paper aims to determine the exact asymptotic classical value of the repeated CHSH game, $	ext{val}_\infty(	ext{CHSH})$, by establishing tight upper bounds.
main_result: It determines that the asymptotic classical rate for the repeated CHSH game is exactly $1 +  rac{\sqrt{5}}{4}$, demonstrating a gap between classical and quantum exponential rates.
method: The authors use relaxation techniques ($	ext{val}^+$) applied to the optimization problem defining the winning probability of the repeated game, reducing it to an elementary optimization solvable via calculus.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on the CHSH non-local game, which is modeled as an XOR game. The results are generalized to show that gaps persist between classical and quantum bounds for any such game.
key_observables: Maximum winning probability ($	ext{val}(G)$), asymptotic classical rate ($	ext{val}_\infty(G)$), and the entangled value ($	ext{val}^*(G)$).
important_parameters: The exponent $n$ (number of repetitions) is crucial for defining the asymptotic limit.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on showing that certain relaxations, like $	ext{val}^{++}(G)$, are sufficient because they can be reduced to one-dimensional solutions without loss of value.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the problem for repeated games, deriving upper bounds using relaxation techniques ($	ext{val}^+$), solving these bounds specifically for CHSH, and concluding with general theorems about the existence of gaps between classical and quantum rates.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete example of quantifying the gap between local hidden variable theories (classical) and quantum mechanics in the context of information theory games, which is fundamental to understanding quantum advantage.
